items.text: Periodical Suffering

"I seem to have stood still for an eternity,"

"Engulfed by a sea of thoughts, kept silent as a cemetery."

"The three lighthouse keepers on the isles still remain,"

"Where they should have long passed into memory."

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: So much has transpired here upon the Flannan Isles, each and every event etching itself into my consciousness ...

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Despite all my installments so far on the History of the Flannan Isles, what I've documented barely scratches the surface ...

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: The readers, I believe, share my eagerness for the next issue of the Daydream Post ...

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: *deep breath* I cannot let them down.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: The young lady rubs her eyes and refocuses back to her writing.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: The History of the Flannan Isles column has to fit in roughly a third of a page ... But there are so many more stories about the archipelago I've yet to tell—stories the readers still haven't heard ...

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Ms. Dennehy mentioned that even the editors have been following the mysteries of the Flannan Isles with intrigue ... If I can keep up that interest, she might allow me an additional section!

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: That way, I can present our readers with a more comprehensive look at their stories.
Livened up, she dives back into her writing.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: "The Flannan Isles, a small island chain in the Outer Hebrides of Scotland, have been the subject of rumor for years. Even up to today, many mysteries still remain here ..."

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: "Of course, to hear it from the credible authorities, the lighthouse and indeed, the whole archipelago, were perfectly normal, all except for ..."

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: "... its three vanished lighthouse keepers."

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: "Speculation over their disappearance drove the public wild, yet the authorities claimed they were simply swept away in a deadly storm."

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: "This, of course, did nothing to convince them."

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: "Meanwhile, a sailor claimed to have seen coal-black UFOs over the islands, casting eerie, cold beams of light ..."

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: "Other theories included gargantuan man-eating birds, a bottomless abyss, and so on ..."

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: "Rumors continue to swirl, but the truth remains elusive ..."

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: "The police report, the log entries, and the lack of any recovered bodies ... They all scream one thing—this is no simple disappearance ..."

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: "Twelve years have passed, yet driven by curiosity, I decided that I must visit the islands myself ... And there I discovered a never-before-seen log book."

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: "The signature on it reads 'James, recorded on December 15, 1900.'"

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Her pen hangs in mid-air, like a sail on still water, hesitating to embark on the next line.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: So much time has passed since the incident, yet the mysteries only seem to multiply ...

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Hmm ... How can I sift through all these story threads?

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Before setting foot on the islands, I heard other unsettling rumors from the sailors. Ships passing too near often find themselves caught motionless on the sea, with eerie and unnatural ooze forming on their decks ... These frightful tales have meant that most give this archipelago a wide berth.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: This is a story worth telling ...

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Meanwhile ... there is the matter of the island's lighthouse, which has, through unknown means, been kept in operation for twelve years despite being abandoned.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: If I failed to include that sort of mystery in my History of the Flannan Isles, I'd surely regret it ...!

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Which, of course, leads to the central mystery of them all. The disappearance of the original lighthouse keepers in the first place ...
Spoiled for choices, Marcus is, nonetheless, in a very briny pickle.
An arduous choice lies before the poor girl.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: History of the Flannan Isles belongs to the islands themselves. It's only fair that I treat their stories impartially ...

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: To turn down the opportunity to tell any of these stories feels like betraying the truth itself!
Her gaze wanders, shifting from one page of notes to another.
There it is, a narrow path that she could follow to capture the essence of all these stories.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: "I set the log book aside, noticing the lighthouse just as its light washes past me."

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: "After the disappearances, no one proved willing to station on the Flannan Isles ... The Eilean Mor lighthouse was left unmanned, or so it should have been."

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: "From the base of the lighthouse, I walk step by step upward. Curiously, I notice, the wooden stairway beneath my feet appears to be meticulously well-maintained, and stranger still is the warm yellow light spilling from the apex of the tower ..."

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: "They all silently, yet truthfully, convey an astonishing revelation: that this lighthouse has been running just as well as it had since it was abandoned twelve years ago!"

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: "My footsteps falter, nearly tumbling backward at the realization ... Yet, how could I believe all that I am seeing?"

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: "Nevertheless, the slippery moss and weathered scratches adorning the grounds prove with cold logic that twelve years must indeed have passed here."

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: "After composing myself, I decide to begin my exploration."

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: "Just before I alighted, I sounded the ship's steam whistle to signal to passing vessels, if there were any. Then, I took the three remaining flares ..."

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: "If misfortune befalls me, at least the maritime police can collect my body here within a week and have my story publicized, if that must be my last humble contribution to the world."

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: "Stepping back onto the island, I no longer feel as relaxed as before; a touch of fear and sorrow occupies me. But thankfully, my heart still harbors the courage to strive for knowledge and human progress ..."

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: "And to unveil the truth of this mysterious place."

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: "Door locks won't bar my way; I deftly climb through a window, entering into a cramped space that, by all rights, should have been long forgotten and moldering."
Marcus has fully immersed herself in the world she is recreating, wandering freely along the blank page, then back to the ink-stained words.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: "The kitchen door is open, though there is naught inside. Not even a moldy apple, a rotten orange, nor even a cobweb."

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: "My mind, as yet stiff with anticipation, suddenly and involuntarily relaxes as it stumbles over an idle thought."

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: "Perhaps this was nothing more than a prank, if a poorly executed one."

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: "Or perhaps a kind-hearted soul, for the safety of all the ships in the area, made a habit of replacing the lighthouse's lamp and repairing its rusty screws, but bowed by some secret honor, swore to never tell any of his work ..."

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: "These are, for now, my best theories on the nature of this mystery."
Marcus wields her pen with renewed fire, drowning out the sounds around her.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: "Out of obligation, I settled on making a final cursory check before leaving."

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: "To think it would mark the beginning of a whole new chapter of this unfolding mystery."

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: "Inexplicably, I found myself knocking on the bedroom door ... Stifling a chuckle, as I soon realized my folly."
"Knock-knock-knock!"

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: "But as I brace to push open the door, it swings open in spite of me with a grating creak."

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: "The sudden movement causes me to stagger and stumble, falling beside the fireplace inside the room."

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: "To my surprise, the coal dust under my palms holds a comforting warmth, as if it had come from a dying flame, one that could again alight."

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: "Two figures form just beyond my vision, at first pale and translucent but gaining substance, as if to match my palpable fear."

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: "Are you ... ghosts?!"

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: "The pair of specters suddenly shriek, as if in terror, 'You can see us?!'"

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: "And we face each other dumbfounded, before a series of knocks come from outside—steady and deliberate."

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: "Knock-knock-knock!"
"Knock-knock-knock ..."
The knocking is no longer just a figment of the author's recollection.
Ms. Marcus ...?
Anyone in there?

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Ah ... Yes. A moment please.
She hurriedly gathers the papers now scattered across the desk, stacking them aside neatly.
Lest the voice outside had grown impatient, she cautiously pulls the door open.
Flannan Isles

items.speaker: Investigator
items.text: Greetings, Ms. Marcus.

items.speaker: Investigator
items.text: The man before her, with his stern gray and neatly patterned tie, nods courteously.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: ... Greetings.

items.speaker: Investigator
items.text: You'll see here I've been sent by the St. Pavlov Foundation. I am the investigator responsible for registering all arcanists in the Eilean Siar region.
His tone is flat and official, but his bearing exudes an air of entitlement and pride.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: The ... Foundation?
The significance behind that name has clearly been lost on the young lady.
TO BE CONTINUED…
